rooms.question: Where does the surface come from if nobody drew its outline?
rooms.ontology: A scalar field assigns values throughout a volume; an isosurface approximates one chosen level.
rooms.action: Circle the glass and wireframe specimen; follow a visible boundary across several triangles before reading its construction.
rooms.observable: An irregular continuous-looking boundary is assembled from small polygon patches.
rooms.mechanism: generate_density_field normalises sampled noise; process_cube reads eight corners, builds an 8-bit case and interpolates threshold crossings before adding table triangles.
rooms.limit: The surface reveals one threshold and one sampling resolution; an empty-looking region still has field values.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Display the same field beside two other thresholds, with seed and sample grid fixed.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified.

rooms.question: What can eight corner samples tell you about the space between them?
rooms.ontology: Corner signs choose a local case; magnitudes locate crossings along edges.
rooms.action: Compare two tiles with different illuminated corners and follow the corresponding triangle edges.
rooms.observable: Fifteen representative cases relate corner samples to local surface patches.
rooms.mechanism: Controller generates densities once for both bead indicators and VoxelChunk; MarchingCubesGenerator extracts with fixed threshold and interpolation.
rooms.limit: Signs do not fully determine geometry between samples. The displayed chunk also includes surrounding cells, and ambiguous cases need conventions beyond a fifteen-picture slogan.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Hold corner signs fixed while changing their distance from threshold, then compare where the edge crossings move.

rooms.question: Can the same surface-making procedure describe a chair and a cup?
rooms.ontology: Field composition separates the description of a shape from its extraction into triangles.
rooms.action: Compare the labelled Chair and Cup specimens; find a junction in one and a hollow in the other.
rooms.observable: Different familiar forms share the same polygon-making apparatus.
rooms.mechanism: Gallery default household roster; TerrainGeneratorShapes selects shader SDF. chairSDF unions boxes;cupSDF subtracts inner cylinder from outer then unions a torus handle.
rooms.limit: A named silhouette does not supply usability, structural strength or human variety. Sampling can erase a thin handle or wall.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Keep the extractor fixed and change one description: thicken the cup wall or remove a chair leg; compare shape and implied use.

rooms.question: Does a repeating surface have to be a pile of repeating objects?
rooms.ontology: A periodic scalar expression can generate connected surfaces without separate pieces.
rooms.action: Follow an opening into a neighbouring fold and change viewpoint when a crossing hides the connection.
rooms.observable: The gyroid-like specimen repeats and bends through three spatial directions.
rooms.mechanism: Compute evaluates sin/cos gyroid expression after noise coordinate warp, then adds erosion and slow thickness terms; threshold extraction follows.
rooms.limit: The placed specimen is a perturbed gyroid-like surface, not an exact minimal surface. Repetition does not guarantee a traversable passage.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Set intrusion to pure before comparing period settings, then restore warp separately.

rooms.question: When two deposits meet, where is their seam?
rooms.ontology: Editing a field changes a surface that will be extracted again; a stroke can be stored as a spatial contribution.
rooms.action: Hold the trigger with the brush inside the sculpting volume to add one short deposit near an existing form; release and inspect the join.
rooms.observable: New rounded material joins the seeded sculpture through a blended boundary.
rooms.mechanism: Controller maps position into generator coordinates andadd_blob appends centre/radius; sculpt shader smooth-combines sphere distances and re-extracts.
rooms.limit: Sampling and blend settings determine which joins remain distinct. Erase mode currently loses its negative sign through abs, so subtraction is unsupported.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Add a clear additive-stroke comparison at two separations before implementing andtesting signed subtraction.

rooms.question: Can a landscape have two surfaces above the same place?
rooms.ontology: A heightfield stores one height per horizontal position; a volume field can also describe interior voids.
rooms.action: Read the top profile, then examine its sides for openings or undercuts. Compare what a top view conceals.
rooms.observable: A terrain-like upper surface belongs to a sampled volume whose default field also includes cave variation.
rooms.mechanism: Flat shader builds terrainDensity from surfaceHeight-worldPos.y andsubtracts weighted3D cave noise; default interior=caverned,caveStrength.4.
rooms.limit: A surface view cannot establish a cave network or a safe route; a thin feature may disappear at coarse sampling.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare the same specimen with interior=none andcaverned, preserving threshold andseed.

rooms.question: How can an opening appear without drawing a doorway?
rooms.ontology: A composed density field can add or subtract spatial tendencies before surface extraction.
rooms.action: Compare a projecting ledge with a recess; use another viewpoint to distinguish a hole from a dark patch.
rooms.observable: The compound terrain combines upper ground, overhangs, caves, arches andoutcrops.
rooms.mechanism: Compute density=baseTerrain-overhangDensity-caveStrength-archStrength+outcropStrength; author landform ladder enables cumulative terms.
rooms.limit: A term named arch is not a guarantee of a doorway. Geometry does not teleport, andfield overlap can close as well as open routes.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Show cumulative hillside,overhung,quarried,arched,compound specimens with common field settings.

rooms.question: What changes when a surface surrounds your viewpoint?
rooms.ontology: Inside/outside is a classification; its embodied consequence depends on orientation, clearance andaccess.
rooms.action: From the available approach, compare the enclosing side of the cave with a view through an opening; follow a boundary visually before attempting a route.
rooms.observable: An irregular cavity makes the surface readable as enclosure rather than a freestanding object.
rooms.mechanism: Cave generator combines ridged multi-octave noise and vertical density bias, thresholds andtriangulates; placed scene noise_scale3.8,iso.88.
rooms.limit: Connected empty samples do not guarantee adequate headroom or collision clearance. The threshold was authored rather than negotiated with each visitor.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Measure a narrow passage against different visitor clearances, andexhibit paired thresholds with common field.

rooms.question: Who designed a corridor when nobody placed its walls one by one?
rooms.ontology: Procedural authors choose field families,scales,biases andthresholds that constrain possible spaces.
rooms.action: Compare the specimen with the previous cave: look for sizes of passages andfrequency of surface changes, without attributing differences to one parameter alone.
rooms.observable: A second cave arrangement is generated from the same family at different scale/threshold settings.
rooms.mechanism: Placed scene noise_scale13.5,iso.85 versus3.8/.88 inside specimen; same noise accumulation andvertical bias.
rooms.limit: Two differing settings do not isolate a cause; randomness does not remove authorship, anda generated void may be inaccessible.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Hold seed,threshold andsampling fixed while changing noise scale, then compare thresholds separately.

rooms.question: Are these blocks moving, or are different blocks being drawn?
rooms.ontology: Changing a sampling offset and rebuilding a representation differs from moving persistent objects.
rooms.action: Watch a small boundary region through several updates; choose a block-sized position andnotice when it appears ordisappears.
rooms.observable: A coarse block arrangement changes as the sampled field offset advances.
rooms.mechanism: Every.2s default rebuildsamples deterministic three-term trigonometric field; cells mode emits a whole cube whenever eightcorners straddle threshold.
rooms.limit: This default view marks boundary-containing cells; it is not an interpolated marching-cubes surface. Rebuilding makes visual motion without preserving a particle identity.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Freeze offset andcompare cells with crossings orfaces at the same resolution.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Actual VR freeze control absent; desktop ui_accept toggles. Do not claim a true4D independent noise function orfluid simulation.

rooms.question: Can two sources make one body?
rooms.ontology: Local influence fields can add to exceed a shared threshold between their centres.
rooms.action: Look for a neck joining rounded regions andcompare its shape with an outer lobe; initial motion may alreadyhave finished.
rooms.observable: Several contributing sources can produce a fused extracted surface.
rooms.mechanism: Metaball generator sumsstrength*radius²/distance² usinginverse_square kernel bydefault, samplesgrid andextracts threshold. It evolves only5steps bydefault before stopping.
rooms.limit: The boundary has no inherent ownership byone source; numerical fields are not material forces. Finite influence culling andsampling shape the result.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Stage two sources at increasing fixed separations with commonthreshold to locate loss of connection.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. Do not promise endless merging animation orvisitor source dragging.

rooms.question: Must a visible surface already exist as a triangle mesh?
rooms.ontology: A field can be queried along viewing rays as well as sampled into a polygon boundary.
rooms.action: Change viewpoint around the moving rounded surface andcompare smooth joins with the prior metaball specimen.
rooms.observable: Blended lobes are shaded as a continuous moving body.
rooms.mechanism: Shader map combines sphere signed distances with smooth minimum; fragment raymarches up to80steps, hit tolerance.001, distance20. No extractedsurface mesh is created; boxmesh bounds display.
rooms.limit: The visible boundary is not automatically collision geometry. Smooth minimum is a different composition from the prior sumofinfluences, so similar appearances can conceal different models.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Place the same distance field beside a marching-cubes extraction at two resolutions andcompare silhouette/collision.
rooms.cautions: Source read only; actual museum runtime, reachability, controls and learner understanding remain unverified. World/local coordinate placement andshader runtime unverified; no touching/collisionclaims.

rooms.question: Can you return by a route different from the one you arrived along?
rooms.ontology: A graph describes intended connections; an implicit shell gives those connections spatial thickness.
rooms.action: Identify an entrance andtrace a possible loop through visible chambers; where passages are accessible, compare a return route with the approach.
rooms.observable: Rounded chambers are linked by passages, with deliberate additional cycles beyond a connecting tree.
rooms.mechanism: Planner scatters chambers, builds minimum spanning tree andextraedges, checksconnectedness/cycle rank; dream_iso mergesbulbs/capsules into wall shell, cuts entrances andextracts colliders.
rooms.limit: Graph connectivity alone does not certify embodied access. Blending, clearance andcollisions canchange which intended connections are usable.
rooms.variation: Proposed extension: Compare graph route andwalkedroute, then change one passage width while holding graph fixed.
